features.label: Age
features.description: Age in years. Coronary risk rises steadily with age.

features.label: Weight
features.description: Body weight in kilograms.

features.label: Height
features.description: Body height in centimetres (the dataset calls this column "Length").

features.label: Sex
features.description: Biological sex recorded in the chart. Men develop coronary disease earlier on average.

features.label: Body-mass index
features.description: Weight divided by height squared (kg/m²). 18.5-24.9 is the healthy range; 25-29.9 is overweight and 30 or more is obese.

features.label: Diabetes
features.description: Diagnosed diabetes mellitus (high blood sugar). Diabetes damages artery walls and roughly doubles coronary risk.

features.label: Hypertension
features.description: Diagnosed high blood pressure (hypertension), a major driver of artery damage.

features.label: Current smoker
features.description: Currently smokes tobacco. Smoking injures the artery lining and promotes clotting.

features.label: Former smoker
features.description: Used to smoke but has stopped.

features.label: Family history
features.description: Family history of heart disease. The dataset does not state the exact criterion; clinically this usually means coronary disease in a parent or sibling at a young age.

features.label: Obesity (BMI > 25)
features.description: Flag recorded by the dataset authors as "Yes if BMI > 25", so it also covers people who are overweight (it matches BMI > 25 for 302 of 303 patients).

features.label: Chronic renal failure
features.description: Long-standing kidney failure. Kidney disease strongly accelerates artery disease.

features.label: Previous stroke
features.description: History of cerebrovascular accident (stroke), a sign of artery disease elsewhere in the body.

features.label: Airway disease
features.description: Chronic lung airway disease such as asthma or COPD (the dataset does not specify which).

features.label: Thyroid disease
features.description: Any recorded thyroid disorder (over- or under-active thyroid; type not specified).

features.label: Dyslipidaemia
features.description: Diagnosed abnormal blood fats (high cholesterol and/or triglycerides, or low HDL).

features.label: Typical angina
features.description: Classic angina - chest pressure brought on by exertion or stress and relieved by rest or nitroglycerin. The single strongest symptom of coronary narrowing.

features.label: Atypical angina
features.description: Chest pain with only some of the features of typical angina.

features.label: Non-anginal chest pain
features.description: Chest pain that does not look like angina (for example sharp, positional or pressing pain).

features.label: Low-threshold angina
features.description: Angina triggered by very little effort, a marker of severe narrowing.

features.label: Shortness of breath
features.description: Breathlessness (dyspnoea) reported by the patient.

features.label: Functional class
features.description: How much symptoms limit daily activity on a 1-4 scale (higher = symptoms with less effort). The source does not say whether the NYHA or CCS scale was used; 0 in this dataset appears to mean no limitation was recorded.

features.label: Blood pressure
features.description: Blood pressure in mmHg recorded as a single number (most likely the systolic, i.e. upper, value - the dataset does not say). Below 120 is normal.

features.label: Pulse rate
features.description: Resting heart rate in beats per minute; 60-100 is the normal adult range.

features.label: Leg swelling
features.description: Swelling (oedema), usually of the ankles or legs, found on examination - can accompany heart failure.

features.label: Weak peripheral pulse
features.description: Weak pulses in the arms or legs on examination, suggesting narrowed arteries outside the heart.

features.label: Lung crackles
features.description: Crackling sounds (rales) heard over the lungs, often from fluid congestion.

features.label: Systolic murmur
features.description: A whooshing heart sound while the heart contracts, usually from a leaking or narrowed valve.

features.label: Diastolic murmur
features.description: A heart murmur heard while the heart relaxes; almost always indicates a valve problem.

features.label: Q waves
features.description: Pathological Q waves on the resting ECG - usually the scar of a previous heart attack.

features.label: ST elevation
features.description: ST-segment elevation on the resting ECG, which can reflect acute or old injury of the heart muscle.

features.label: ST depression
features.description: ST-segment depression on the resting ECG, a sign that heart muscle may be short of oxygen (ischaemia).

features.label: T-wave inversion
features.description: Inverted T waves on the resting ECG, which can indicate ischaemia or strain.

features.label: Left ventricular hypertrophy
features.description: ECG signs of a thickened left heart chamber, often caused by long-standing high blood pressure.

features.label: Poor R-wave progression
features.description: R waves that fail to grow across the chest leads, which may point to an old anterior heart attack.

features.label: Bundle branch block
features.description: A delay in the heart's electrical wiring on the left (LBBB) or right (RBBB) side. LBBB in particular is associated with underlying heart disease.

features.label: Fasting blood sugar
features.description: Blood glucose after an overnight fast. 70-99 mg/dL is normal; 100-125 is pre-diabetes and 126 or more suggests diabetes.

features.label: Creatinine
features.description: Blood creatinine, a waste product cleared by the kidneys; higher values mean weaker kidney function. Normal is roughly 0.6-1.3 mg/dL (lower in women).

features.label: Triglycerides
features.description: Fasting blood triglycerides (a type of fat). Below 150 mg/dL is normal.

features.label: LDL cholesterol
features.description: "Bad" cholesterol that builds plaque in artery walls. Below 100 mg/dL is optimal.

features.label: HDL cholesterol
features.description: "Good" cholesterol that helps clear fat from arteries. Below 40 mg/dL (men) or 50 mg/dL (women) increases risk.

features.label: Blood urea nitrogen
features.description: Blood urea nitrogen, another kidney-function marker; normal is about 7-20 mg/dL.

features.label: ESR
features.description: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate, a general marker of inflammation. Normal upper limit is about 15-20 mm/h and rises with age.

features.label: Haemoglobin
features.description: Oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells. Normal is about 13.5-17.5 g/dL in men and 12.0-15.5 g/dL in women; low values mean anaemia.

features.label: Potassium
features.description: Blood potassium, important for the heart's electrical rhythm; normal is 3.5-5.0 mEq/L.

features.label: Sodium
features.description: Blood sodium; normal is 135-145 mEq/L.

features.label: White blood cells
features.description: White blood cell count per microlitre, a marker of infection or inflammation; normal is about 4,000-11,000. (The source paper writes the unit as "cells/ml"; the values match cells per microlitre.)

features.label: Lymphocytes
features.description: Lymphocytes as a percentage of white blood cells; normal is about 20-40 %.

features.label: Neutrophils
features.description: Neutrophils as a percentage of white blood cells; normal is about 40-70 %.

features.label: Platelets
features.description: Platelet count in thousands per microlitre (clotting cells); normal is about 150-450.

features.label: Ejection fraction
features.description: Share of blood the left ventricle pumps out with each beat, measured by transthoracic echocardiography. Normal is about 52-72 % (ASE/EACVI 2015; the lower limit is 54 % in women); 41-49 % is mildly reduced and 40 % or less is reduced (a weak heart muscle). This dataset records EF in 5 % steps.

features.label: Regional wall-motion abnormality
features.description: Echo finding of heart-wall segments that move abnormally, coded 0-4 in the dataset (0 = none; higher = more extensive, exact coding not documented by the authors). It describes wall motion, not the location of a blockage.

features.label: Valvular heart disease
features.description: Severity of any heart-valve disease seen on echocardiography.

targets.label: Coronary artery disease
targets.territory: Whole heart - at least one major coronary artery with >= 50 % diameter narrowing
targets.description: Overall probability that coronary angiography would show at least one major coronary artery (LAD, LCX or RCA) narrowed by 50 % or more.

targets.label: Left anterior descending artery
targets.territory: Anterior wall, anterior two-thirds of the septum and the apex of the left ventricle
targets.description: Probability of >= 50 % narrowing somewhere in the left anterior descending artery or its branches.

targets.label: Left circumflex artery
targets.territory: Lateral and posterolateral walls of the left ventricle (and the inferior wall in left-dominant hearts)
targets.description: Probability of >= 50 % narrowing somewhere in the left circumflex artery or its branches.

targets.label: Right coronary artery
targets.territory: Right ventricle, inferior wall and inferior septum (via the posterior descending artery in right-dominant hearts) and, in most hearts, the sinus and AV nodes
targets.description: Probability of >= 50 % narrowing somewhere in the right coronary artery or its branches.
